'''Shisho Shrine''' (四所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen|ja|城崎温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Onsen}}, {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en|Toyooka, Hyōgo|qid=Q696388|lt=Toyooka, Hyōgo}}, adjacent to the {{ill|Goshono-yu|ja|御所の湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshono-yu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135540751}}, one of the town’s prominent hot springs.

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines:
* {{ill|Yuyama-nushi no Kami|ja|湯山主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuyama-nushi no Kami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as the primary deity.
* The {{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|ja|宗像三女神|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Sanjoshin|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses}}—{{ill|Tagorihime|ja|多紀理毘売命|2=ja|3=タキリビメ|4=fr|5=Takiribime|6=zh|7=多紀理毘賣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|多岐都比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タギツヒメ}}, and {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵島比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime||2=fr|3=Ichikishimahime|4=ja|5=イチキシマヒメ|6=zh|7=市寸島比賣命|8=ru|9=Итикишима-химэ|10=de|11=Ichikishima-hime}}—are also worshipped as protective deities of the hot springs and water.

== History ==
The shrine’s origins trace back to {{ill|Wadō (era)|en|Wadō (era)|qid=Q1373026|lt=Wadō era}} 1 (708), when a local official named Nisei Shimo Gongen received a divine revelation in a dream from four deities. In {{ill|Yōrō|en|Yōrō|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yōrō era}} 1 (717), the monk {{ill|Dōchi|ja|道智|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōchi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} visited the shrine and received an oracle that led to the establishment of the {{ill|Mandarayu|ja|まんだら湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mandara-yu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135540745}}, the first hot spring bath in Kinosaki. Since then, the shrine has been revered as the guardian of Kinosaki Onsen. During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu Hanzenrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1970535}} in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the shrine separated from its affiliated temple, {{ill|Onsen Temple|ja|温泉寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11562939}}, and was officially designated a village shrine in 1873.

Behind the main hall, a spring known as "Enmei-sui" (Life-Prolonging Water) flows continuously.

== Festivals ==
* '''Kinosaki Onsen Festival''' (April 23–24): Commemorates the memorial day of the monk Dōchi, the founder of Kinosaki Onsen.
* '''Kinosaki Dream Plaza''' (July 23–August 25): Evening festivities, including small booths and performances, are held in the shrine precincts, with nightly fireworks (except August 10–16).
* '''Kinosaki Danjiri Festival''' (October 14–15): A traditional festival with portable shrines and floats.

== Shrine Structures ==
The current shrine structures were rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 3 (1928) after the original buildings were destroyed during the {{ill|1925 North Tajima earthquake|en|1925 North Tajima earthquake|qid=Q11401118|lt=1925 North Tajima Earthquake}}. The {{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=Honden}} is a {{ill|Sangensha Nagare-zukuri|ja|三間社流造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sangensha Nagare-zukuri|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and the worship hall is an {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|qid=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri}} structure, both registered as cultural properties of Hyōgo Prefecture. The original main hall, constructed in {{ill|Kan'en|en|Kan'en|qid=Q1145723|lt=Kan'en era}} 4 (1751), was made entirely of zelkova wood and was significantly larger.

* Worship Hall (registered December 22, 2006)

=== Toyooka City Designations ===
'''Cultural Properties:'''

'''Natural Monuments:'''
* Habitat of {{ill|Euterpnosia chibensis|lt=Himeharuzemi|ja|ヒメハルゼミ|ceb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Euterpnosia chibensis|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5976326}} (a cicada species).

== Access ==
* 15-minute walk from {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen Station|en|Kinosaki Onsen Station|qid=Q1055689|lt=Kinosaki Onsen Station}} on the {{ill|San'in Main Line|en|San'in Main Line|qid=Q1135170|lt=Sanin Main Line}}.

'''Shisho Shrine''' (四所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto Shrine}} located in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}{{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en|Toyooka, Hyōgo|qid=Q696388|lt=Toyooka City}}. It is situated adjacent to the public bath "Gosho no Yu", one of the baths of {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen|ja|城崎温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Onsen}}.

== Deity ==
'''{{ill|Yuyama-no-Okami|ja|湯山主大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuyama-no-Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (ゆやまぬしのかみ) is enshrined as the principal deity, accompanied by the deities 
{{ill|Tagorihime|ja|多紀理毘売命|2=ja|3=タキリビメ|4=fr|5=Takiribime|6=zh|7=多紀理毘賣命|lt=Takikuri-hime (多岐里比売神)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takikuri-hime-no-kami|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, 
{{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|多岐都比売命|lt=Takitsuhime (田記津比売神)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takitsuhime-no-kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タギツヒメ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10932592}}, and 
{{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵島比売命|lt=Ichikihime (市杵比売神)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime-no-kami||2=fr|3=Ichikishimahime|4=ja|5=イチキシマヒメ|6=zh|7=市寸島比賣命|8=ru|9=Итикишима-химэ|10=de|11=Ichikishima-hime}}
of the {{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|ja|宗像三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Three Goddesses|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses}}, thus enshrining the Four Shrine Gods. All are revered as guardian deities of {{ill|Onsen|en|Onsen|qid=Q655311|lt=Onsen}}, and the {{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|ja|宗像三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Three Goddesses|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses}} are additionally venerated as water guardian deities.

== History ==
In the 1st year of {{ill|Wadō (era)|en|Wadō (era)|qid=Q1373026|lt=Wado}} ({{ill|708|en|708|qid=Q23511|lt=708}}), a man named Nichisei Shitagenokami founded the shrine in accordance with a divine oracle ({{ill|Oracle|en|Oracle|qid=Q217123|lt=Oracle}}) delivered by four deities in a dream. In the 1st year of {{ill|Yōrō|en|Yōrō|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yoro}} ({{ill|717|en|717|qid=Q23532|lt=717}}), a divine oracle was received by {{ill|Dōchi|ja|道智|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōchi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, who visited the shrine, and he is said to have inaugurated the public bath "Mandara-yu". Since then, the shrine has been venerated as the guardian of {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen|ja|城崎温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Onsen}}, with the Onsen-ji temple established by Dōchi ({{ill|Onsen-ji Temple|ja|温泉寺 (豊岡市)|lt=Onsen Temple|lt_ja=温泉寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onsen-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11562944}}) serving as its head temple. However, under the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏判然令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu Bunri Decree|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1970535}} of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} era, the shrine separated from that temple in the 3rd year ({{ill|1870|en|1870|qid=Q7741|lt=1870}}) and was reclassified as a village shrine in the 6th year.

A renowned spring, "Enmei-sui", issues forth from behind the main shrine.

== Festivals ==
* {{ill|Kinosaki Onsen Festival|ja|城崎温泉祭り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Onsen Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – {{ill|April 23|en|April 23|qid=Q2527|lt=April 23}} to {{ill|April 24|en|April 24|qid=Q2529|lt=April 24}}: Held in commemoration of the anniversary of the enlightenment of Dōchi Shōnin, the founder of Kinosaki Onsen.
* Kinosaki Onsen Dream Plaza – {{ill|July 23|en|July 23|qid=Q2722|lt=July 23}} to {{ill|August 25|en|August 25|qid=Q2819|lt=August 25}} (excluding Obon and weekends/holidays, from 20:00 to 21:00): Various events such as super ball scooping, food stalls, and performance shows are held within the shrine precincts. Additionally, during this period, approximately 200 "Dream Fireworks" are launched for 5 minutes beginning at 21:00 (excluding {{ill|August 10|en|August 10|qid=Q2779|lt=August 10}} to {{ill|August 16|en|August 16|qid=Q2812|lt=August 16}}).
* {{ill|Kinosaki Danjiri Festival|ja|城崎だんじり祭り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinosaki Danjiri Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (festival) – {{ill|October 14|en|October 14|qid=Q2922|lt=October 14}} (Yoimiya) to {{ill|October 15|en|October 15|qid=Q2919|lt=October 15}} (Main Shrine)

== Shrine Buildings ==
The current shrine buildings were completely destroyed and burned along with ancient records in the 14th year of the {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō}} era ({{ill|1925|en|1925|qid=Q18107|lt=1925}}) during the {{ill|1925 North Tajima earthquake|en|1925 North Tajima earthquake|qid=Q11401118|lt=Kita-Tajima Earthquake}}, and were rebuilt in the 3rd year of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} era ({{ill|1928|en|1928|qid=Q19715|lt=1928}}). The {{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=Main Shrine}} is constructed in the Sanmen-sha style, and the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=Worship Hall}} is a single-story building with a hip-and-gable roof; both are designated as tangible cultural properties of the prefecture. In the 56th year of the Shōwa era ({{ill|1981|en|1981|qid=Q2437|lt=1981}}), renovations were carried out under the design and construction of {{ill|Wada Masaharu|ja|和田政春|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Masaharu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Incidentally, the former main shrine was an expansive structure built entirely of zelkova (keyaki), dating from the 4th year of the {{ill|Kan'en|en|Kan'en|qid=Q1145723|lt=Kan'en}} era ({{ill|1751|en|1751|qid=Q7615|lt=1751}}).

Natural Monument:
